job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

passage: Teacher: Today, let us discuss the properties of whole numbers. Rohan, if we subtract 3 from 7, we get 4. If we subtract 7 from 3, do we get the same result? Rohan: Yes, teacher, subtraction is commutative like addition. Teacher: Actually, that is a common error. 7 minus 3 is 4, but 3 minus 7 is not a whole number at all. Subtraction does not follow the commutative property. Priya: What about the identity element for subtraction? Is it zero, like in addition? Teacher: No, Priya. In addition, adding zero to a number leaves it unchanged, so zero is the additive identity. However, subtracting zero from a number is different from subtracting a number from zero. Therefore, zero is not the identity element for subtraction. Remember, whole numbers start from zero, while natural numbers start from one. On the number line, numbers to the right are always greater than numbers to the left. If you subtract a larger number from a smaller one, you move left past zero, which takes you out of the set of whole numbers. Always check the order of your numbers carefully before performing operations to avoid these mistakes.

items.evidence: 7 minus 3 is 4, but 3 minus 7 is not a whole number at all.
items.q: Meena works out 9 − 5 and then 5 − 9. What does she find?
options: Both give 4, since order never matters
Both give whole numbers, just different ones
items.explain: Like 7 − 3 and 3 − 7, changing the order changes the answer; 5 − 9 is not whole.

wrong.why: thinks a − b is the same as b − a
thinks subtracting whole numbers always gives a whole number
reverses which subtraction leaves the whole numbers

items.evidence: However, subtracting zero from a number is different from subtracting a number from zero.
items.q: Priya checks 8 − 0 and 0 − 8. What do her two answers show about zero?
options: It is the identity for addition, not subtraction
It is the identity for subtraction as well
It gives the same answer in either order
It is the first natural number we count
items.explain: 8 − 0 is 8 but 0 − 8 is not, so zero is not subtraction's identity.

wrong.why: thinks zero is the identity for subtraction
thinks subtraction order does not matter
thinks the smallest natural number is 0

items.evidence: Remember, whole numbers start from zero, while natural numbers start from one.
items.q: How do the whole numbers differ from the natural numbers?
options: Only the whole numbers contain zero
Only the natural numbers contain zero
Both sets contain zero, so they match
Neither set contains zero at all
items.explain: Whole numbers start from zero, but natural numbers start from one, so only whole numbers include zero.

wrong.why: thinks the two sets are the same

items.evidence: If you subtract a larger number from a smaller one, you move left past zero, which takes you out of the set of whole numbers.
items.q: Aman starts at 2 on the number line and subtracts 5. Where does he end up?
options: Left of zero, outside the whole numbers
At zero, since the line ends there
Right of zero, still a whole number
items.explain: Taking a larger number from a smaller one moves you left past zero, out of whole numbers.

wrong.why: thinks the number line stops at 0
thinks subtraction always stays in whole numbers
